newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST-Poll positive on key Danish firm profits.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Poll positive on key Danish firm profits.

text.p: A panel of Danish share analysts polled by Reuters on Monday presented overwhelmingly positive profit estimates for selected major Danish companies for the period 1996-98 since the last poll in October.

VThe panel of bank and brokerage firm analysts downwardly adjusted their average 1996 expectations for only three of the 10 firms in the survey, cleaning group International Service System A/S (ISS), food, drinks and packaging group Danisco and (marginally) telecommunications group Tele Danmark.
The downward adjustments were minus 12.1 percent for ISS, minus 5.4 percent for Danisco and a minimal minus 0.2 percent for Tele Danmark compared to the October poll.

The panel upped estimates markedly for Denmark's two biggest banks Den Danske Bank (plus 14.3 percent) and Unidanmark (13.5 percent) and holding company Sophus Berendsen (11 percent), leaving expectations for the other companies more or less unchanged.
Following are forecasts for the 1996 and 1997 profit before tax and extraordinary items of 10 Danish blue-chip companies.
The estimates were made by seven banks and brokerage firms polled by Reuters (millions of crowns).

The forecasts were made by Den Danske Bank, Jyske Bank, Aros Securities. BG Bank, Bjoernskov & Co, Svenska Handelsbanken and Den Koebenhavnske Boers. The two banks first mentioned made no forecasts for banks and BG Bank did not estimate its own result. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen Newsroom +45-33-969652
